summary: In international space launch developments, China successfully orbited its secretive TJS-27 satellite pair alongside a next-generation Tianlian relay satellite, while SpaceX launched 24 Starlink satellites from California. In military space acquisitions, the U.S. Space Force selected 15 companies for a $981 million contract pool to build training capabilities and awarded K2 Space $22.9 million for a laser communications demonstration, while Spain committed up to $2.3 billion for national military communications supporting Europe's IRIS² constellation. For civil space operations, Japan's space agency announced its probe achieved the closest-ever flyby of an asteroid, NASA opened a new Flight Dynamics Research Facility in Virginia, and NASA partnered with SpaceX on wind-tunnel testing for Starship while planning a future two-probe mission to evaluate complex lunar three-body orbits. In scientific developments, astronomers using artificial intelligence identified seven quasars that could explain supermassive black hole growth, planetary scientists found solar winds accelerate Martian atmospheric ion loss, and preliminary research suggests moonquakes may help reveal buried ice at the lunar south pole. Looking ahead, space officials are evaluating scheduling options as NASA determines future flight opportunities for the Starliner-1 mission.
